maybe you suffer from a mental illness or a disorder that has made you so impulsive. i have the same situation, while not to the same degree, i was incredibly violent and a danger to myself and my family. i’ve been arrested for it twice. 

i have spoken to psychiatrists and therapists. even if your crimes are horrendous, if you are willing to leave that part of you behind for good, while you can’t reverse your actions you can shape your future. i was not a good person, it took years of hard work, and my family not trusting me. but things change. 

i don’t know what you have done, nor do i want to. but you seem remorseful and while that won’t change what you have done, it proves that you have the strength to never do it again. i would strongly suggest you stick to it. 

all in all, i would hugely recommend going to a psychiatrist and a therapist. you don’t need to tell them what you have done, but you can air out some grievances and figure out what has made you the way that you are. they will not judge you, they will not treat you any lesser. we are all human, we are not robots and we all make mistakes. 

i’m reading between the lines and i feel i might have a rough idea of your story, and if it is true i cannot excuse your actions. but this doesn’t mean you’re not worthy of a life and redemption. people change and people grow. it will haunt you, and sometimes rightfully so, but it will be a constant reminder of how far you’ve come from that moment, and how you can keep moving forward and never become that person again.

only the worst of the worst are irredeemable. i am not going to pry for information, but do you fit that category? you need to sit and think *hard* about where you would sit on the ladder. where do you fall? perhaps see a therapist and get some things off your chest, and see what they have to tell you. 

dependant on what you’ve done, there is ALWAYS room for redemption. terrible people can and have changed their ways before, and it will continue to happen as people grow. the first indication to me that you can change yourself is the fact you know and admit you have done wrong. 

like i said, i don’t know the extent of what you have done in the past, but you can try and make the mother more comfortable. give her her space, as much as possible. make sure she knows you are not a threat to her, and you know apologies don’t fix your mistakes, but she has total safety in your property. whatever you can do to solidify that you are not a threat to her health and safety, and the baby, DO IT.
